content.content:
# Member API

Every handler returns `{ status, body }`. Clients match on the strings in `messages`, so their wording is part of
the contract and must not change.

## Conventions

- Email addresses are matched case-insensitively. They are stored trimmed and in lowercase, whether they belong
  to a user or to an invitation.
- Names are stored trimmed and may be at most 80 characters.
- Roles are `owner`, `admin`, `member` and `viewer`.
- When validation fails the status is `400` and the body is `{ "error": "validation_failed", "messages": [...] }`.
  Every failing field adds one message; the order is email, name, role.
- `404` is `{ "error": "not_found", "message": "user not found" }`, `409` is
  `{ "error": "conflict", "message": "email already in use" }`.

## Validation messages

| Field | Rule | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| email | missing, not a string or blank | `email is required` |
| email | not of the form `local@domain.tld` | `email is invalid` |
| name | missing, not a string or blank | `name is required` |
| name | longer than 80 characters | `name must be at most 80 characters` |
| role | not one of the roles above | `role is invalid` |

## POST /users (createUser)

Body: `email`, `name`, optional `role`. The role defaults to `member`. Responds `201` with the user. Answers `409`
when a user with that email exists.

## PATCH /users/:id (updateUser)

Accepts partial input: only the fields that are present are validated and changed, and a field that is present is
held to the same rules as when creating. A body without any of the three fields is rejected with the single
message `no fields to update`. Answers `404` for an unknown id and `409` when the email belongs to another user.
Responds `200` with the updated user.

## POST /invitations (inviteUser)

Body: `email`, `role`, optional `name`. The invitee fills in their name when they accept, so the name may be
missing or empty (it is then stored as an empty string); a name that is given must still be at most 80
characters. The role is required (`role is required`) and `owner` cannot be granted by invitation: it is rejected
with `role is invalid`. Answers `409` when a user or a pending invitation with that email exists. Responds `201`
with the invitation, which has the status `pending`.

## GET /users (listUsers)

Query: `q` (matches name or email), `limit` (1 to 100, default 25), `offset` (default 0). Invalid paging values
answer `400` with `limit must be between 1 and 100` or `offset must be 0 or greater`.

## DELETE /users/:id (deleteUser)

Responds `204`. Answers `404` for an unknown id and `409` with `cannot delete the last owner` when the user is
the only owner.
# member-api

Request handlers for the member directory API: creating, updating, inviting, listing and deleting users.
Handlers are plain functions that take the in-memory store and a request and return `{ status, body }`; the
HTTP layer that calls them lives in another repository.

The behavior clients can rely on, including the exact error messages, is described in `docs/api.md`.

## Layout

- `src/handlers/` one file per endpoint
- `src/response.js` helpers that build `{ status, body }` results
- `src/store.js` the in-memory store
- `src/routes.js` the route table
- `test/` tests, one file per handler

## Tests

Node 20 or newer, no dependencies to install:

```
npm test
```

content.text:
The email, name and role checks now live in one place, `src/userValidation.js`, and all three handlers use it. A future fix only needs to be made there.

**How it works**
- There are three functions: `validateEmail`, `validateName` and `validateRole`. Each returns either the cleaned-up value or the error message clients already receive. I kept the message wording exactly as before, since `docs/api.md` says clients depend on it.
- Where the endpoints genuinely differ, the difference is now an explicit option instead of a separate copy:
  - Invites call `validateName(..., { required: false })`, because the name is optional there.
  - Invites call `validateRole(..., { allowed: INVITABLE_ROLES })`, so `owner` can't be granted by invitation.
  - Create still defaults the role to `member`, and update still only checks fields that are present. Both are handled in the handler before calling the shared check.
- Error messages still come out in the order email, name, role.

**One behaviour change: an existing bug got fixed**
`inviteUser` trimmed emails but never lowercased them, even though `docs/api.md` says invitation emails are stored in lowercase. In practice:
- An invite to `ANN@example.com` went through even when `ann@example.com` was already a user.
- The invitation was stored with its original capitals.

The shared check always lowercases, so that's fixed now. I added a regression test for it and confirmed it fails against the old `inviteUser` code. Any invitations already stored with capitals will stay that way; this change doesn't touch existing data.

**Tests**
- New `test/userValidation.test.js` with unit tests for each check, including the 80-character name limit and the allowed-roles list.
- Two new tests in `test/inviteUser.test.js`: the lowercase regression test, and one confirming the `owner` role is rejected.
- `npm test` passes: 23 tests, 0 failures (16 before this change).

I haven't committed anything.
